findings.title: F1 is presented as the owner's call but the design decides it, and silence reverses amendment 1
findings.target: Opening note, line 3; overrule list, lines 32-33; R20/storage notes, line 184; role table, lines 227-228; R48 C_node, line 343; Comparison 2, lines 534-539; section 12 F1, lines 545-547
findings.argument: Amendment 1 (v1 lines 126-143) records the owner's own word: one child researches and then reviews in the same session, with the field still in its context. A fresh reviewer is used only past the 300k ceiling. Amendment 3 part E.3 refused to reverse this without him. Version 2 reverses it in four places while section 12 still calls F1 his decision. (1) Line 3 says v2 replaces amendment 1's rules. (2) The role table has no review role for the child; only a 'Fresh reviewer' role exists (lines 227-228). R8 makes the fresh review the normal path (line 98). (3) The pack's node capacity C_node = W_quality - P - R_rev (line 343) only exists if a fresh reviewer reads the pack, so the B+ layer itself presupposes the fresh path. (4) Section 12 sets the silent default to 'both run, and no difference shown defaults to fresh' (line 546-547). Comparison 2 then makes that default near-certain. It scores three plants with n = 1 per arm, which can only show a gap above |R1 - R2|. It also counts 'judgment share' as a secondary. That share is penalised by construction, because line 184 labels every same-window sentence JUDGMENT. The experts may favour fresh (D3-13, D8-07), but D4-08 says only 'whichever form is chosen'. Recommending is allowed; deciding by default and by the label rules is not.
findings.smallest_fix: Line 3: amendment 1 stands until the owner rules on F1. Section 12: the silent default is amendment 1 (the same session reviews; fresh past the ceiling), plus D4-08's 'the fresh path runs at least once per wave'. Comparison 2 drops 'judgment share' as a secondary and uses D8-07's count of factual sentences that cite nothing in the frozen pack. Add a 'child (reviewing)' row to the role table, conditional on F1.

findings.title: F2: the mapper's second expert becomes the silent default, and the owner's form is never measured
findings.target: Section 12 F2, lines 548-550; P-table F2, line 446; layer 4 Later list, lines 286-287; Comparison 2, lines 534-536
findings.argument: Amendment 1 point 4 (v1 lines 140-141), on the owner's word: a second expert is a second child doing its own research from the same question list. Amendment 3 E.3 recorded 'a second reviewer of the same pack' as a reversal that was not made. Version 2 makes it the silent default: 'then a second reviewer of the same pack plus the contrary-evidence reader'. Version 2 also drops the one mapping that would measure the owner's form. D6-10 proposes, for the pilot, a partly crossed design: pack A reviewed twice, plus one review of a pack B made by an independent research run. That design would show whether the variance between packs exceeds the variance between reviewers. Version 2 keeps only R2, 'a second fresh review' of pack A (line 535), and moves second-opinion to Later (line 286). So 'measure before buying' (line 446) measures only the mapper's option.
findings.smallest_fix: Silent default: no second expert until the owner rules; if he rules for one, it is amendment 1's form. Replace 'R2 a second fresh review' with D6-10's partly crossed design (pack A twice, plus pack B from an independent research run) when the pilot allowance covers it. Otherwise state that F2 stays unmeasured.

findings.title: The seven measures appear nowhere, so the owner has no path to see them for the tree
findings.target: Whole document; owner page, lines 55 and 167; R46, lines 320-321; section 11, lines 511-531
findings.argument: The owner judges everything by throughput, efficiency, token count, token cost, time taken, quality and hallucinations. The word 'seven' does not occur in v2, and neither do 'throughput' or 'hallucination'. Version 1 had a ledger rule 'so the programme can report its own seven measures' (v1 rule 6, line 100-102); v2 drops it. The 'owner page' view is named but never defined. R46 'every measure has an action line' does not say which measures. R19's 'measure' field is not tied to the seven. Section 11's parameters are execution internals (Δ, T_box, σ), not the seven. Comparison 1's secondaries hold fragments: tokens, time, citation failures and confirmed answers per million tokens. No script computes the seven, so nobody runs them. The experts' effect_on_measures field on every mapping is also dropped, so no rule says which measures it moves or costs.
findings.smallest_fix: One pilot rule with a runner. render.mjs computes the seven per task, field, wave and arm from the transcripts and the ledger. Throughput = approved ids covered by a witnessed or confirmed card per hour. Efficiency = confirmed answers per million tokens. Token count = transcripts, helpers included. Token cost = the count weighted by the measured price ratios, with no currency. Time taken = ledger timestamps, sleep gaps shown apart. Quality = Comparison 1's primary plus the blinded rubric. Hallucinations = witness and checker rejections, citation failures and the seeded escape rate. They go on the owner page. R46's action lines and Comparison 1 report these seven. R19's measure field is that enum. Add a 'measures moved' column to section 9 from the mappings.

findings.title: R8's checkpoint lets a fenced attempt's uncommitted output spread into the next attempt
findings.argument: R8 builds the checkpoint from 'last commit record plus the dead attempt's schema-valid objects', read after the fence. The model check found exactly this as flaw F1. NoStaleAccepted fails with every mechanism present, and no fault is needed: a planned hand-over fences e1, e1 writes cards before it is stopped, and restore copies them into e2, which commits them. It also contradicts R15 (outputs visible only through a commit record) and line 127 ('recovery reads commits'). D2-03 restores from committed items only. This is the owner's requirement (d) failing at its core: a zombie's output becomes trusted lineage.
findings.smallest_fix: R8: at the fence, replace.mjs records the attempt's journal high-water mark in the task row (leader-epoch truncation, the model's FIX_RESTORE_CUT). The checkpoint is the commit records plus only the objects at or below that mark, read after the stop is confirmed. Those objects re-enter as untrusted staging through commit.mjs.

findings.title: Overflow is still 'cut and list the rest' on the path that actually fires: the spend limit
findings.argument: R49 claims to 'replace cut the pack and list the rest' with the tree's own operations. Yet R12's hard limit, which is the node's capacity in the frame, fences the child, 'the task cut, its uncovered ids kept'. Nothing routes those ids to R49(d)'s overflow leaf. R49(e) 'only the owner drops a range' has no runner. D2-02's on_failure is also dropped: an overflow range that is neither scheduled nor dropped by name blocks the synthesis gate. So uncovered ids can silently end as 'not covered', which is the withdrawn amendment-3 behaviour. In the pilot every t_q is a prior. The R49(a) hook therefore decides on invented numbers, and D2-02's 'no estimate means overflow' is missing, so the R12 cut is the likely path. After a split (R49d, R50), one field has two leaves. Nothing writes the new range boundary into tree-plan.json (the parent), and nothing says which pack the field's review reads. A B+ split always updates the parent.
findings.smallest_fix: R12's cut writes an overflow record {ids, tokens, reason}, and replace.mjs turns it into R49(d)'s overflow leaf. The split writes the separator into tree-plan.json. gate.mjs refuses the synthesis while any range is neither committed, scheduled, nor dropped on the owner's quoted word. The field's review reads both leaves through R18's two-level index. In the pilot, log the predicted against the realised t_q per group, so that R49(a) is measured and not trusted.

findings.title: The square-root law, which counts tokens only, replaces the owner's 300k ceiling for the research child without asking
findings.target: Overrule list, lines 36-37; R51, lines 354-358; layer 6 notes, line 377; section 12, lines 568-569
findings.argument: The owner's core idea (amendment 1 points 1, 3 and 5) is a child that fills its window with checked knowledge and keeps the field in context, with a 300k ceiling as the exception. R51 makes the child hand over at W*. cost.js puts W* at about 115k-155k, with 8-15 hand-overs per field (adaptive k). So no session ever holds the field. The law prices only token count. Line 377 concedes that 'a hand-over's quality loss has no token price', and D3-01 says the formula does not price it. Quality is one of his seven measures, and the trade is never shown to him: section 12 offers the hand-over measure only as 'token count or weighted cost' (line 569). This is a decision on his word, not a borrowed solution.
findings.smallest_fix: Section 12 adds 'the research child's hand-over point', with the silent default being amendment 1's 300k ceiling. W* still governs the coordinator and helpers. The pilot logs hand-overs per field and reads them against Comparison 1's quality primary. Add 'quality' as a third option of the hand-over measure.

findings.title: Five more model-check flaws are absent, and section 9 claims residuals the model already refuted
findings.target: R6, lines 89-91; R7, lines 92-94; R9, lines 99-102; R11, lines 106-110; R58, lines 400-404; section 9 rows N3, N5, N9
findings.argument: The model check of the execution layer has already run. Its six SPEC flaws break the owner's requirement (d), a structure where a mistake cannot spread, yet v2 carries none of the five that are not already A4-04. F2: a lost wake after the watcher's own urgent exit is permanent; R7's endturn does not cover it, and NoDeadlock fails in 5 steps. F3: pause detection works only inside one live watcher (R6), so a healthy field is restarted and charged. F4: endturn starts a second watcher, which breaks the ledger's single writer. F5: R9 'parks it for the owner, slot freed' without a fence or a stop, so the failed attempt keeps spending. F6: R11 counts 'sessions run', not live processes. R58 still names as its 'first case' a stale-coordinator wake that the model shows is already held by the --ce fence. Rows N5 ('None known') and N9 ('Model check to confirm') read as open where the answer exists.
findings.smallest_fix: One-line changes, each with its basis. R6: the stall clock is the watched non-paused time persisted in watcher.json (FIX_CLOCK). R7: a Task Scheduler re-wake while the events seq exceeds acked_seq, stored in coord.json (FIX_REWAKE). R4: a watcher.lock with its pid (FIX_ONE_WATCHER). R9: fence and stop before parking (FIX_STOP_ON_FAIL). R11: count live processes (FIX_COUNT_LIVE). R58: state that its properties must first be strengthened (count COMMIT creations, recoverable stalls, R = 1, the 4-event budget) before 'holds' counts.

findings.title: 'Experts first' has no gate between research and review; expertise is certified only after the review is spent
findings.argument: Amendment 1 point 3: 'It is checked, then it reviews.' In v2 a review task is admitted when its dependencies are 'committed' (R11). Committed means schema-valid, not covered or trusted. R45's certificate bundles the expertise checks (coverage, confirmed cites, reads) with the review checks (SPRT, plants) and runs after the review. So a review can start on a pack that covers few approved ids or is mostly unverifiable. The raw-opinion failure the owner set out to prevent is then detected only after its tokens are spent.
findings.smallest_fix: Split R45. Gate A (admit.mjs, before a review task) requires every approved id covered by a witnessed or confirmed card or listed not covered, R36 coverage above the owner's floor, and the unverifiable share under its R46 line. The certificate after the review keeps the SPRT and the plants.

findings.title: The fresh reviewer's input set, which defines what the expert knows, has no named writer
findings.target: Layout, line 56; R14, lines 137-139; role table, line 228
findings.argument: review-in/<task>/ is the reviewer's whole context, and the owner's requirement (a) hinges on it: checked knowledge, no hopes, no coordinator opinion (v1 section 5.3). R14 names a writer for every store but not for review-in/ or queue/. The coordinator holds Write, so by default it assembles the reviewer's context. That reopens P2 anchoring, and the coordinator's own reading spreads into every review. R23 audits reads against in/ but cannot tell whether in/ itself was right.
findings.smallest_fix: Add to R14: replace.mjs builds review-in/<task>/ from the frozen pack hash, the must-read snapshots and the field's fixed file list in protocol.json, and writes nothing else. guard-hook denies the coordinator's writes there.

findings.title: The coordinator's square-root hand-over needs the owner every ~18 coordinator calls; time and owner presence are not priced
findings.target: R13, lines 115-118; R51, line 356; section 12, lines 557-558
findings.argument: cost.js gives the coordinator k* = 17.6 calls and W* = 133k. R13 needs the owner to start each successor from a one-line brief, because notes go to whoever started the child. The owner is not continuously present (harness fact 11), so the whole tree idles at every coordinator hand-over. H0 counts tokens only. Time taken and throughput, two of the seven, carry the real cost, and section 12 states it as 'so it stays'.
findings.smallest_fix: R51 for the coordinator: past W*, hand over at the owner's next message, with a hard stop at the recorded quality line. The pilot logs the owner's start latency, and time taken shows it.

findings.title: The B+ bulk load can never place a key: field-prefixed ids and fixed lanes reduce it to a check on priors
findings.argument: Keys are '<field>-<group>-<nn>' (R47), so a key's leaf is fixed before plan-tree runs, and 'leaves start as the lanes; a lower bound checks them' (R48). D2-01's load orders ids by mechanism tag and fills leaves to f times C. It reruns after the pilot with measured t_q, and an id with no estimate blocks the wave. Version 2 runs it once on priors and gives no rerun. So the plan-time split, the one B+ operation that avoids paying for research and then cutting it, rests on guesses, and the real splits happen late through R49 and R50.
findings.smallest_fix: R48: plan-tree.mjs reruns on unit-costs.mjs's measured t_q before wave 1. A lane over f times C splits by group range then, before spend. Ids with no estimate are listed and block admission (D2-01 on_failure). Say once that at seven leaves the borrowed parts are capacity, fill factor, key-range split and never dropping a key.

findings.title: The owner's pilot sits behind about 35 scripts and some 15 thresholds whose silent default is 'nothing runs'
findings.target: Section 10, lines 480-498; section 12, lines 562-565; section 13, lines 587-588
findings.argument: 56 of 59 rules are marked pilot. Section 12 makes every threshold (d0, p1, β, the SPRT's p0, p1, α, β, plants, coverage floor, residual, effects, an action line per measure) a precondition, and silence means 'no gate can run, so nothing is admitted'. The mappings already give defaults (d0 0.8, p0 0.05, p1 0.20, α = β = 0.05 in R43-R44). One pilot field cannot calibrate SPRT or Clopper-Pearson rates in any case (14 seeds per J class plus clean items). Time taken and throughput are the owner's measures, and his 'pilot field first' (amendment 2 C) is starved.
findings.smallest_fix: Silence on a threshold means the mapping's stated default, logged as such. Move R36-R37 (coverage and certainty grading need more than one field), R39's seeded refuter and R44's SPRT to Later. The pilot keeps execution, commit, witness, seeds, measures and the two comparisons.

holds: Fencing by equality with the task table plus the coordinator epoch --ce (R2) is distributed systems used properly: the model check's TwoCoordinatorsAct holds and fails when --ce is ablated.
Progress instead of liveness (R5) and level-triggered wakes (R7) are real borrowings: ablating either breaks LoopEventuallySuspected or AlwaysCanResolve in the model.

Visibility only through an exclusive-create commit record (R15), consumers reading only commits, nothing edited in place, citations as foreign keys pinned to a pack hash (R18, R19): matches D2's whole design.
R18 'no confirmed card is cut', with the pack going out of line as a two-level index, follows the B+ rule that a key is never dropped (D2-02 do_not).
R50 separates a roll-over from a split and bounds hand-overs with n_max (Denning's thrashing), the use of the square-root law that D3-01 asks for.
The witness as a script over our own snapshot (R26) addresses P21 and the owner's demand for checked knowledge; two trust grades (witnessed and confirmed) do not overstate what a script certifies.
Agreement never raises a claim (R38) and a dismissal is an open hazard with a bar (R39): a review that is not a raw opinion, without same-model voting.
Section 8 states the completeness estimate as a stop signal, not a number, matching the analysis's own caveats.
Section 12 does list F1 and F2 as the owner's decisions, and section 13 is candid about what is believed and what is unverified.
The left-out list correctly refuses B+ height, latches, B-link and underflow merges at seven leaves (D2 do_not).
result.overall: Version 2 is a real advance as engineering. Its fencing, commit records, progress watchdog, frozen packs and never-drop overflow are borrowed whole and mostly used properly. Against the owner's four requirements it falls short in three places. First, it decides two things amendment 1 records as his word. F1 is decided by the role table, the B+ capacity formula, the JUDGMENT labels and a silent default of fresh review, all under a comparison that can hardly overturn that default. F2 makes the mapper's same-pack second reviewer the default and drops D6-10's design that would have measured his form. A third point on his word is the research child's hand-over: the token-only square-root law replaces his 300k ceiling without asking. Second, the seven measures appear nowhere and no script computes them, so the owner has no path to see them for the tree. Third, mistakes can still spread. R8 carries a fenced attempt's output into the next attempt, which is the model check's NoStaleAccepted failure, and five more flaws the model already found are absent. On the B+ tree, 'cut and list the rest' survives on the spend-limit path and the bulk load runs on priors with field-prefixed keys, though out-of-line packs and the roll-over-versus-split rule are genuine. The fixes are small and mostly about defaults and runners. Make amendment 1 the silent default for F1, F2 and the child's ceiling. Add one script that renders the seven measures. Cut the restore at the fence mark. Route R12's cut into an overflow leaf, with a gate that blocks the synthesis.
